title: A 15-vertex counterexample to the odd-kernel conjecture for io-decomposable Riordan graphs
exact_endpoint: Riordan.source_conjecture_false : ¬ SourceConjecture (finite Definition 2.9, canonical odd copy) and Riordan.source_conjecture_false_infinite_family : ¬ SourceConjectureInfiniteFamily (every integer series a with a_0 odd and a_(2j+1) ≡ a_j mod 2, every n ≥ 2, singular G_n(a, za), every real 0-eigenvector has zero odd part)
scope: Cheon, Jung, Kitaev and Mojallal, Riordan graphs II: Spectral properties, arXiv:1801.07021v1 (journal accepted manuscript in the Strathclyde repository retains it), Conjecture 7.7: for a singular io-decomposable Riordan graph G_n(g, zg), X_o = 0. False: g = 1+z+z^3+z^6+z^7+z^8+z^12+z^13 at n = 15 gives a connected io-decomposable Bell Riordan graph of nullity 1 whose kernel vector has odd part (-1,0,-1,0,1,0,1,1); the same graph arises from an infinite series satisfying the Lemma 2.11 identity at every index.
substantive_reason: It refutes a published conjecture formulated from Sage experiments, robustly under both the finite definition and the source's infinite coefficient characterization; the witness is minimal (n = 15) within the infinite-recurrence family by exhaustive search and is not a classical Pascal or Catalan graph; the failure mechanism (cancellation C x_o = -B x_e) is not excluded by the source's rank theorem.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; not worldwide priority
remaining_literature_limits: final publisher body unread (accepted manuscript read)
Spectral properties of Pascal graphs body not obtained
trust_limits: minimality within the recurrence family and nullity are ordinary computation, not Lean claims
not_claimed: The finite-definition n = 7 twin example as a result
